method: fresh shallow clone of the pinned commit; read the pacing, retry, cache, finance, report, pagination and auth code, then froze the 429 handler against the donor itself

coverage.read: amazon_mcp/clients/rate_limit.py, http_retry.py, response_cache.py (all); sp_api.py lines 154-280, 600-630, 703-945; auth/lwa.py 1-90; ACCEPTANCE.md 1-80
coverage.not_read: the remaining ~1,000 lines of sp_api.py, ads_api.py, tiktok_api.py, meli_api.py, tools/*, cogs, dag, monitor, connectors, refiner, middleware, 64 test files, docs; gateway modules named by tests are absent from the snapshot
coverage.statement: Bounded semantic review of the files named, not the whole source. No extinction is claimed.

rows.behaviour: One token bucket per SP-API category (orders 1/60 s, reports 1/45 s, inventory 2/s burst 5, products 5/s burst 10, catalog 2/s, finances 0.5/s, default 2/s) chosen by path prefix; every call acquires a token first (proactive pacing).
rows.failure_semantics: a path outside the prefix table silently uses the default bucket
rows.configuration: rates are constants in the file
rows.ecdev_today: The SP-API transport reads the rate the API itself reports (x-amzn-RateLimit-Limit) per operation, records minimum_next_request_ms, and refuses a request before that time (official_http_throttle_preserves_receipt_and_denies_early_retry).
rows.knowledge: The donor hard-codes category rates from documentation at one point in time; ECDEV follows the rate the API reports per operation and per response, which also covers an operation absent from the table. Divergence is deliberate: a constant table goes stale, a reported limit cannot.
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: not needed: documented limits are per operation and change; no oracle can freeze them

rows.behaviour: On a 429 the handler reads Retry-After with float() and raises RateLimitError; call_with_backoff retries up to 6 attempts with delay min(8 s, 0.25 s doubling), but never less than Retry-After, which may be any length.
rows.failure_semantics: a Retry-After that is an HTTP-date, or any non-number, raises ValueError out of the handler instead of throttling; inf, nan, negative, exponent and 1e+20 values are honoured as given
rows.ecdev_today: retry_after_not_before reads the RFC 9110 grammar (delta-seconds, IMF-fixdate, RFC 850, asctime) with saturation; a throttled request is not retried automatically but denied until retry_not_before_ms.
rows.knowledge: Pinned on 20 header values run through the donor handler: it accepts "+7", "-1", "1.5", "1e3", "inf", "nan", "" (waits 1 s) and 99999999999999999999 (1e+20 s), and raises ValueError on all three HTTP-date forms, so a legal 429 turns into an unhandled exception. ECDEV waits on the valid grammar only and never guesses. Not adopted: automatic retry with doubling backoff; ECDEV surfaces the not-before time to the caller instead of sleeping inside a tool call.
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answered: frozen oracle compared and pinned

rows.behaviour: An in-process dict with a per-category TTL (pricing 300 s, inventory 600 s, catalog 900 s, sales 3600 s, default 300 s); at 2000 entries the oldest inserted key is dropped (insertion order, not recency); a TTL of 0 stores nothing.
rows.failure_semantics: a stale entry is deleted on read; nothing is revalidated
rows.ecdev_today: Fetch results are cached by HTTP freshness (Cache-Control, Expires, validators; 24 h cap; compared with Scrapy this wave) up to 256 MiB; seller responses are not cached across restarts.
rows.knowledge: The donor TTLs are product choices with no stated basis and no revalidation; ECDEV takes freshness from the origin and keeps the evidence of when a value was observed. Nothing to absorb.

rows.behaviour: Finances v0 events are summed into revenue (Principal charges), fees by type (Commission/ReferralFee, four FBA types, everything else "other") and refunds (Principal adjustments only), as Python floats rounded to 2 decimals, with abs() applied to every fee.
rows.failure_semantics: an unrecognised fee type is counted as "other", not flagged; a refund of tax or shipping is dropped; a missing amount is 0.0
rows.ecdev_today: Money is typed minor units in a stated currency; fee assumptions in estimates are explicit and labelled estimated; seller financial reads are a restricted domain, disabled by default.
rows.ecdev_real_caller: no: seller finances are disabled in ECDEV
rows.knowledge: Float money, abs() on fees (a fee reversal becomes a charge) and silent classification of unknown fee types are exactly what ECDEV types out. Fee-type vocabulary (Commission, ReferralFee, FBAPerUnitFulfillmentFee, FBAFees, FulfillmentFee, FBAWeightBasedFee) is noted as reference for the day a seller-side financial read is enabled.

rows.behaviour: Reports are requested (POST /reports/2021-06-30/reports with type, marketplace and window), polled by id until a document id exists, then the document is fetched through a pre-signed URL and gunzipped for a 50-line preview.
rows.failure_semantics: the pre-signed URL is fetched with a plain client (no size bound, no host policy, 120 s timeout); gzip.decompress is unbounded; text is decoded with errors="replace", so a corrupt byte becomes U+FFFD silently
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV has no report reads. It now has a bounded, CRC-checked native gzip decoder (adapter/web/src/gzip.rs) that rejects the corruption classes Python accepted.
rows.knowledge: If a seller-side report read is ever enabled, the shape is create, poll, resolve document, download, decompress. The three weaknesses above are the specification of what to do differently: bound the download, bound the inflate, decode strictly. Needs a credentialed seller account to test and the restricted-domain decision.
rows.evidence: source read; gzip behaviour pinned by gzip_oracle.rs
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: blocked: needs credentials and a product decision

rows.behaviour: NextToken is passed back to the caller as next_token / nextToken and re-sent on the next call; the client never loops.
rows.ecdev_today: Social and feed sources page by their own cursor with a request budget, repeated-cursor stop and coverage reporting.
rows.knowledge: Single-page pass-through; ECDEV already walks cursors under a budget and reports coverage. Nothing further.

rows.behaviour: Refresh-token flow; a token is refreshed when under 300 s remain; the access token and expiry are written to a shared file (mode 0600) keyed by a hash of the client id.
rows.failure_semantics: a cache write failure is ignored; the token sits in plaintext on disk
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV never writes tokens to disk, never uses a grantless or expired token, and tests the refresh and expiry contract (lwa_refresh_and_expiry_contract_never_uses_grantless_or_expired_tokens).
rows.knowledge: The 300 s early-refresh margin is the same idea ECDEV applies. Writing the access token to a file is refused by ECDEV's secret boundary.

rows.donor_source: amazon_mcp/tools/*, cogs/*, dag/*, monitor/*, connectors/*, refiner/*, gateway-oriented tests
rows.behaviour: Seller-account operations: restock and IPI reports, reimbursements, account health, cost-of-goods store, alert thresholds, a task DAG executor, cross-platform snapshots, billing and API-key gateway tests (several tests import gateway modules that are not in this snapshot).
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV is a market-research engine; seller account operations are a restricted domain and disabled.
rows.knowledge: Account-bound seller operations, outside ECDEV's research scope. Listed so the corpus is known, not read in depth.

rows.behaviour: Clients for Amazon Ads, TikTok and Mercado Libre APIs.
rows.knowledge: Other platforms' authenticated APIs; not reviewed. Mercado Libre and TikTok shop data would be new sources if ever wanted.
